answer.justification: The patient presents with the classic triad of hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis. The presence of hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis despite treatment with an ACE inhibitor (lisinopril), which typically increases serum potassium, strongly suggests primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome). In this condition, excessive aldosterone production leads to increased sodium reabsorption, potassium excretion, and hydrogen ion secretion, resulting in the observed laboratory abnormalities.
